name: The Birth of the Blessed Virgin Mary
dates: Feast · Kept in Rome from the seventh century
history: Nine months after the Immaculate Conception, the Church keeps the birthday of the Mother of God. A saint’s feast usually marks the day of death, the birthday into heaven, but the liturgy celebrates the earthly birth of only three: Christ, His Mother and Saint John the Baptist. The feast began in the East and was kept in Rome by the seventh century.
life: Scripture says nothing of Mary’s birth. The names of her parents, Joachim and Anne, come from the Protoevangelium of James, a second-century writing that the Church never received as Scripture but whose stories passed into art and devotion. The feast probably began in Jerusalem with the dedication of a church near the Pool of Bethesda, honoured as the site of her parents’ home, where the Crusader church of Saint Anne still stands. It spread through the East and was kept in Rome by the time of Pope Sergius I, at the end of the seventh century, who ordered a procession for it. Saint Andrew of Crete and Saint John Damascene preached on it. The liturgy sees in her birth the dawn before the sunrise: the child born today will bring forth the Saviour of the world.
prayerTo: Holy Mary, the Church sings that your birth announced joy to the whole world, because from you would come Christ, the Sun of justice. Pray for every child born today, for mothers awaiting birth, and for me, that the grace God began in you may also be brought to completion in me. Amen.
penance: Pray today for a mother expecting a child, or give to a charity that supports women through pregnancy and early motherhood.
meditation: The liturgy compares Mary’s birth to the dawn before sunrise. Where in your life might God be preparing a dawn you cannot yet see?
prayer: Bestow upon Your servants, we beseech You, O Lord, the gift of heavenly grace, that, as the child-bearing of the Blessed Virgin stood for the beginning of our salvation, so may the solemn feast of her Nativity bring about an increase of peace. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
